label: early copy step (recall 1-2) of long sequences when re-input token is 3/e/c/u/t/x
explanation: Very sparse, tiny-magnitude reset-gate unit (0.03% of steps, max 0.007). Fires only in the copy phase at t=10-11, i.e. recall_idx 1-2 (80% of mass at recall_idx 2, when the fed-back input is orig(1)), almost exclusively for L=9 (88% of mass) or L=8. Never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, at recall_idx 0, or at recall_idx >= 3. The fed-back input token is the main driver: digit 3 (54% of mass, strongest examples) and e (23%), then c, u, t, x; never fires on a, b and many other letters. The predicate covers ~96% of activations and ~98% of mass, but precision is only ~3%: most steps matching these conditions do not fire. Adding the output token (u, 3, j, o raise the rate) or the previous token gets precision to ~20% at the cost of recall, so firing seems to depend on a further token-specific conjunction that a simple rule does not capture. Largest activations: input 3 at recall_idx 2 in L=9 sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=3 (+3.30), phase=2 & in_tok=c (+3.07), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+2.72), recall_idx=2 & in_tok=3 (+2.72), phase=2 & in_tok=e (+2.70), t=10 & prev_tok=<DEL> (+2.17).
